rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing (ban on sale and use of algorithmic rent-setting devices)
rules.requirement: Under this proposed ordinance, San Diego landlords could not use software that relies on nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels, and no one could sell or license such software to landlords. A tenant could sue a violating landlord for an injunction, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: Civil penalty up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation

coverage.summary: All residential rental property in the City of San Diego. Excludes software that publishes reports from public data or from aggregated nonpublic data more than 90 days old without recommending future rents, and software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Software used to establish rental rates or income limits under local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines

rules.exemptions: Excludes (a) software that publishes reports on rental rates or occupancy from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or from public information, and does not recommend rents or occupancy for future leases or renewals; and (b) software used to establish rental rates or income limits under local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: Tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and reasonable attorney's fees. Each month of use and each property is a separate violation. Remedies are cumulative.
rules.quoted_span:
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

notes: The document is a February 2025 staff report and draft ordinance (O-2025-107). The ordinance number, date of final passage, and adoption certification are blank, so it is recorded as pending. The text would take effect 30 days after final passage. A reviewer should verify whether the Council adopted it and on what date; if adopted, the status would likely be in_force. The sale/licensing ban (§ 98.1103(a)) and the landlord-use ban (§ 98.1103(b)) are captured in a single record.
